note: Maps what a visitor is trying to do, and what a guide is about, to IntelliTools utilities that really exist. Verified against tools.js, v2-tools.js, v21-tools.js and the tools/ pages by tests/knowledge-tool-map.mjs; a tool that fails verification is never recommended. 'phrases' are exact triggers (the first six tools keep their original lexicon phrases). 'intents' are rules: every group in a rule must match (a rule is AND of OR-groups over word stems), so a lone shared keyword never fires a tool. Rules and topics are not used for 'what is ...' or comparison questions. 'topics' recommend the tool beside a confident answer on those guides, only for how-to or general questions, with 'topicWhy' explaining the link. A tool never replaces a Knowledge answer.

tools.name: AI Prompt Builder
tools.reason: Use it when you are drafting a prompt. It walks through role, request, context, process, tone and output, then assembles one prompt you can copy. It does not call a model.
tools.topicWhy: This guide explains the ideas. The builder helps you apply them by assembling role, context and output format into one prompt you can copy.

tools.name: Prompt Diff
tools.reason: Use it to compare two prompt versions and see which lines were added or removed. It does not measure whether the model got better.

tools.name: Fact Anchor Checker
tools.reason: Use it to check claims in an answer against source text you paste. It is a manual spot-check, not a way to stop hallucinations in general.

tools.name: PII & Secret Redactor
tools.reason: Use it to mask emails, phone numbers and API-key-like strings before you paste text anywhere. Pattern matching is not exhaustive, so read the result.
tools.topicWhy: Before you paste customer or internal text into an AI tool, the redactor masks emails, phone numbers and API-key-like strings in your browser.

tools.name: Agentic Workflow Generator
tools.reason: Use it when you already know you want a workflow and need roles, handoffs, inputs and guardrails written down. It does not explain what an agent is, and it does not run the workflow.
tools.topicWhy: When you are ready to use the pattern, the generator writes down the roles, handoffs, inputs and guardrails for your own workflow.

tools.name: JSON Formatter
tools.reason: Use it to validate and pretty-print JSON in the browser. It does not design a schema or call a model.
tools.topicWhy: To try this on your own data, paste it into the formatter to check that it parses and to pretty-print it.

tools.name: Image Studio
tools.reason: Use it to resize, convert or compress an image in your browser without uploading it. It does not edit what is in the picture.

tools.name: Private PDF Tools
tools.reason: Use it to merge, split, rotate or shrink a PDF in your browser, so the file is never uploaded. It does not edit the text inside a PDF.

tools.name: OAuth & JWT Claim Decoder
tools.reason: Use it to read the claims and expiry in a JWT and to review OAuth scopes, all in your browser. Decoding a token does not prove its signature is valid.
tools.topicWhy: To look inside a real token, paste it into the decoder to read its claims and expiry locally.

tools.name: Env Diff
tools.reason: Use it to compare the keys in two .env files and spot missing or drifted ones without showing the secret values. It does not check that a value is correct.

tools.name: cURL Token Stripper
tools.reason: Use it to strip credentials from a cURL command and get a safer fetch example. Pattern matching is not exhaustive, so read the result before sharing it.

tools.name: SQL & Mock Data Builder
tools.reason: Use it to turn a simple schema into a CREATE TABLE statement and a JSON mock record. It does not run SQL or look at your real database.

tools.name: Base64 Encode / Decode
tools.reason: Use it to encode or decode UTF-8 text as Base64 in your browser. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption.

tools.name: Timestamp Converter
tools.reason: Use it to convert Unix timestamps and ISO dates in your browser. It runs locally and does not read timestamps out of a log for you.

tools.name: Cron Humanizer
tools.reason: Use it to read a five-field cron expression in plain English and flag obvious collisions. It does not run or schedule anything.
